speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Cassandra Lee and Mr Yip asked how Singapore officers in Malaysia would handle individuals found to be carrying items controlled or prohibited under Singapore law, such as drugs or vapes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The traveller in question would be handed over to the Malaysian authorities and the case would then be handled in accordance with Malaysian law and their position on offences on drugs and non-compliant vapes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But regardless of how Malaysian law deals with such attempts, our focus is to harden our borders against such items and prevent them from coming into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, we will do so when we have the ability to do checks, both at Bukit Chagar Station as well as at Woodlands North Station.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As Singapore officers are not granted powers of arrest when they are performing their duties in Malaysia, Ms Lee is correct to say that our officers would need to seek assistance by leveraging existing mechanisms and channels between both countries' law enforcement agencies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We cannot arrest in Malaysia and Malaysian officers cannot arrest in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Should drugs be found or, in fact, any other illicit items be found during checks done in Singapore, Singapore law would then apply.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And Singapore's zero-tolerance approach to drug trafficking will not change.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Yip asked about deployment of officers to the other country during what paragraph 7 of the Second Schedule refers to as "serious unplanned incidents".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have mentioned earlier, this is a contingency, with the intention to provide for an expeditious but a controlled way of deploying additional manpower in appropriate cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I understand the point that Members have made about the urgency of the situation: Mr Tan mentioned fires, Mr Yip mentioned incidents and every second counts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We endeavor to strike a balance between that urgency and the propriety of both officers who respond to such incidents from both sides.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Lee asked how the co-located CIQ model of the RTS Link compares with co-located border control in other countries.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: One distinct feature of the RTS Link is where immigration clearance takes place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For the RTS Link, the traveller goes through departure and arrival clearances before embarkation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is similar to the experience at the Channel Tunnel, which connects the UK and France, which Ms Lim also alluded to.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: A different approach, however, is taken for the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In that case, a traveller departing Shenzhen goes through departure and arrival clearances only upon disembarkation in Hong Kong.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To return to Shenzhen – the reverse journey – he goes through departure and arrival clearances in Hong Kong before boarding the train.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I wish to assure this House that the model adopted for our RTS Link is the subject of quite extensive deliberations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We discussed internally, as well as bilaterally with Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Obviously, the system has got to find consensus on both sides to be able to be equally applicable on both sides for this to work.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ultimately, I want to assure the House that the aim is to provide a travel experience that is smooth and seamless, as many have articulated, but at the same time, strictly without compromising on safety and security, especially of our border controls.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Vikram and Dr Neo Kok Beng asked whether there will be security personnel on board the RTS Link trains.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are no plans to deploy our enforcement officers on board the trains, but there will be comprehensive CCTV coverage of the interior of the train cabins that will be monitored back-end in real-time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The rail operator also has the option of deploying roving staff on board trains, as and when they decide necessary and they will be able to contact the operations control centre and provide any necessary assistance during the five-minute journey.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: A few Members raised questions about concurrent criminal jurisdiction and cross-border incident management.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In particular, Ms Lee, Mr Yip and Ms Sylvia Lim, asked about the method by which Singapore and Malaysia would determine the country with primary right to exercise jurisdiction over criminal offences on board a train in transit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I mentioned this earlier in my opening speech, but I thought I will just repeat some of these points.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, therefore, if an offence is committed on a train that is journeying from Bukit Chagar Station to Woodlands North Station, then Singapore would have primary right; and the converse is true.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Earlier, a Member said, what happens if you break down halfway and you are towed back to your original station, then I suppose the destination will be where you are towed back to.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And in that scenario, that would be the country that has the primary jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Should the offence be committed on a reverse journey, I think I do not need to repeat that, Members understand that it will be the converse on what I have just said earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, where there is public interest for us to conduct investigations into the matter, Singapore may request for Malaysia to waive its right.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have not hard-coded what public interest might look like, because each scenario could well be different and it depends on the context, the different circumstances on which the case arises and the way in which we might view our interest in a particular offence or the individual concerned.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we have not hard-coded that into the framework here, but there is an arrangement within the Bilateral Agreements.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would say also that it is not only in the context of such an arrangement where we have co-located the CIQs, that issues of public interests might arise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, it arises all the time when there are cross-border incidents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And Members know that we have one of the busiest cross-border land checkpoints at the Causeway and we have been managing this with the Malaysians consistently.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there will be no change to that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The law enforcement agencies of the country with the primary right to exercise jurisdiction will work closely with the rail operator to gather and preserve any available evidence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is the method and I want to emphasise that both countries have discussed and agreed on in the RTS Link Supplementary Agreements; and both sides have an obligation, under those agreements, to abide by it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are situations where one country may well want to assert jurisdiction, but there is also a process for countries to discuss, if both assess that there is public interest in prosecuting the case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would just like to remind this House that our Bill applies to cross-border railways generally.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not just limited to giving effect to the bilateral arrangements for this particular RTS Link with Johor, with Bukit Chagar.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is purpose-built to accommodate similar treaties for other cross-border railways, if and when they arise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We cannot foresee the precise details of those cross-border railways, whether there might be a co-location of CIQ or how the parties might take jurisdiction of the trains in the manner which I have articulated earlier; and therefore, our approach has been to espouse the broad principles on criminal jurisdiction in the Bill itself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I have mentioned earlier, some of the specifics that relate to the RTS Link in this case appear in the two Schedules that I have taken Members through earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Malaysia, which Ms Lim had taken the trouble of looking up the legislation, has taken a different approach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members will see that, in fact, the Malaysian Bill specifically mentions Singapore-Johor Link and it is designed specifically for this Link only.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that is why they have enacted an RTS-specific legislation which codifies the specific arrangements that we have agreed to bilaterally in our agreements in their Bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, they have taken a different approach from us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are important principles and they help determine the country that would have overall command and control of the management of a cross-border incident and ensure that both countries' responses are coordinated and do not pose unnecessary risk to friendly forces.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Both sides have also addressed other operational aspects of cross-border incident management via a comprehensive set of joint SOPs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These were developed with the rail operator's involvement, so that all the relevant stakeholders around such an incident that might occur, can work in tandem to respond effectively to such incidents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Yip had an additional question on ensuring officers' accountability during cross-border incident management.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I had taken Members through earlier, what these limits would look like in my opening speech as well as earlier in my reply speech.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When discharging their duties, be it managing cross-border incidents or even carrying out routine duties at the CIQ zone, all officers remain under the order of their commanding officers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is provided for under clauses 13, 22, 30 and 34 of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Turning now to data protection, Ms Lee asked how the provisions regarding data protection would be operationalised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Dennis Tan had asked whether the data that we collect, when transmitted back to Singapore, would be protected or secured and he asked whether it would be air-gapped.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we have a secure line that transmits that data.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Lee also asked how the Government would hold relevant parties accountable in the event of a data breach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Since the data is collected, transmitted, kept and governed under Singapore law, any data breach would, therefore, be dealt with in accordance with Singapore law – something we are familiar with.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If the incident is a result of bilateral obligations relating to data protection and inviolability of equipment not being complied with, then the Government will consider all available legal and diplomatic options, in accordance with the bilateral RTS Link treaties, as well as the relevant international law.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This Bill gives effect to a very comprehensive set of arrangements that facilitate co-located CIQ clearance and undergirds jointly developed protocols for coordinated management of cross-border incidents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This will, in turn, help to ensure that the RTS Link experience for travellers is not only convenient and seamless, but also safe and secure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On that note, I thank the Members' support of this Bill, and Mr Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications arising out of the Minister's response?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
text: I would just like to ask the Minister what is the main reason of not having security on board?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as a default, we do not propose to start with having dedicated security personnel on the trains.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This is in relation to when Singapore may have to give up its primary jurisdiction to Malaysia to investigate incidents and particularly on clause 39(2).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: As I mentioned in my speech, there are three conditions to be satisfied if we were to give up primary jurisdiction and one of them is that it must also be the case that Malaysia has no obligation to cede jurisdiction to us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, I had turned it up to the same page; I thought the Member might ask that question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Clause 39, if the Member has it with her, deals with a scenario where we take jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, if you look at clause 39(1), "Any conduct engaged in by a person   on board a...train...   defined zone  ,... if engaged in within Singapore, would constitute an offence...   treated... as if the person engaged in that conduct in Singapore." So, clause 39(1) is a provision that takes jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member might recall that I talked about the trains, which direction, where the nose was and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so that is the framework that determines the jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is in that context that we put in a provision that talks about a reference to when they might cede jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because otherwise, they would have jurisdiction over all matters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, even if it appears that an incident happened within the framework of what might be Malaysia's jurisdiction, but if the individual or the offence is not a subject of proceedings, then the conditions are not satisfied.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope this makes it quite clear.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: There being no further clarifications, I will put the question to the House.      .
